scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator introduces a wave of 'all time great' animated TV dramas that are currently being overlooked.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Something kind of amazing is happening right now but most of you are missing it. There's been a wave of some all time great TV dramas but they happen to be animated.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen: SOMETHING KIND OF AMAZING IS HAPPENING RIGHT NOW BUT MOST OF YOU ARE MISSING IT

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator highlights 'Common Side Effects' on Adult Swim and Max.
scene_timeline.audio_description: The most recent one is called Common Side Effects and it airs on Adult Swim and/or Max.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen: COMMON SIDE EFFECTS NEW SERIES FEB 2 [adult swim]

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator references his previous praise for 'Scavengers Reign' on Netflix.
scene_timeline.audio_description: I previously talked about Scavengers Reign on Netflix, which I consider to be one of the all time great single seasons of TV.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator mentions 'Pantheon' on Netflix as another masterpiece.
scene_timeline.audio_description: And more recently I've talked about Pantheon, which got two seasons and did get to complete its story. It's also on Netflix, it has an all star cast, beautiful animation.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator claims these animated shows surpass many 'prestige TV' live-action dramas like Breaking Bad.
scene_timeline.audio_description: But I think these shows are better than most of the live action shows that aired during the golden era of 'prestige TV' dramas.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator defines 'adult' content as exploring the sensation of existing in unfixable systems.
scene_timeline.audio_description: I mean that they all address the very adult sensation of existing in a system that you don't know how to fix and so you kind of don't know what it means to be a good person in that system.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator summarizes the plot of 'Common Side Effects' involving a miracle mushroom cure and its conflict with corporations.
scene_timeline.audio_description: It's about this guy who is a genius but kind of a hippie who lives off the grid. And he discovers a mushroom that can cure anything. And his goal is to get this miracle cure out to the people, but to him that means keeping it away from the evil pharmaceutical corporations.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator notes the involvement of Mike Judge and the 'Scavengers Reign' team.
scene_timeline.audio_description: This show has a lot of people working on it that worked on Scavengers Reign. And also Mike Judge who has done of course King of the Hill and Silicon Valley.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator explains the show's nuance regarding the difficulty of growing the miracle fungus naturally.
scene_timeline.audio_description: It turns out that this guy's miracle fungus is rare not due to any kind of conspiracy or evil, but just because it's difficult to grow. It requires certain soil and a certain climate.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator discusses the bureaucratic and corporate requirements for mass-producing a cure.
scene_timeline.audio_description: The thing that he wants... can only happen if it is mass produced on an incredible scale at incredible expense with layers of bureaucracy and quality control, stuff that could only be supplied by some huge institution.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator reflects on the realization that holding power makes idealism difficult.
scene_timeline.audio_description: You watch as this guy has the realization that every idealistic adult has... 'I am screwing things up in the exact same way.' Being on the outside of a system and critiquing it is easy... actually being in control of the system and doing it better is a million times harder.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator compares the theme of corrupting power to Robert Baratheon in 'Game of Thrones.'
scene_timeline.audio_description: This is what I loved about Game of Thrones when it came out because it started with the story of a revolutionary who then got the reins of power and was just as corrupt.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator emphasizes that building a better system is harder than being a disruptor.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Being a revolutionary or disruptor is extremely difficult, but actually building up a system, a better system that works for everybody, is a million times harder.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator praises the hyper-realistic animation style and subtle character expressions.
scene_timeline.audio_description: All this is conveyed with an animation style that's kind of hyper-realistic and has all these extremely subtle facial expressions and mannerisms. It just really conveys the authenticity of these characters.

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator concludes that these shows are part of a remarkable, now-ending animation boom.
scene_timeline.audio_description: I get the sense that all of these shows are part of a post-pandemic animation boom that is now over. But if so that's too bad because a lot of what came out of it was remarkable.
